Why is Krishna called Damodar? Dam means rope. Udar means belly. The one with a rope around his belly. As the story goes, little Krishna broke a pot of butter and fed it to the monkeys.
Mother Yashoda caught him and decided to tie him to a heavy grinding stone. She took a rope. Two fingers too short. She added another rope. Still two fingers too short.
She tied every rope in the house. Always two fingers short. Wait, how is that possible? He was God. No rope can hold him. But when he saw his mother tired and sweating, he let himself be tied.
One finger is her effort. The other is his grace. That's why he is Damodar. He can only be held by love. Comment Damodar if you light a lamp this Kartik.
